chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Al-Sakhar Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim, raised it to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) looked at the people on the Day of Fitr playing and laughing, so he said to his companions and turned towards them: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the month of Ramadan as a race track for His creation so that they might compete in His obedience to achieve His Pleasure. So a group preceded in it and succeeded, and others were left behind and failed. So the wonder, the utmost wonder, is from the laughing and playing ones on the day in which the do-gooders are rewarded and the deficient ones lose out. And I swear by Allah! If the covering were removed, the good-doer would be occupied with his goodness and the evil-doer with his evil.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about people playing and laughing on the Day of Fitr?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of a 'racecourse' (midmaran) to frame Ramadan as a competitive spiritual endeavor, highlighting the stark contrast between those who secured divine favor and those who fell short. He critiques the frivolous laughter of Eid as a sign of spiritual negligence, asserting that the reality of individual accountability is so profound that if the veil of the unseen were lifted, people would be too absorbed in their own deeds to engage in idle play. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on transitioning from the communal worship of Ramadan to the sustained mindfulness of the self in daily life.
